canonical: track-me-web/tests/fixtures — copy to each client, same as group-status-vectors.json
note: SCOPE_1.8.7 §6.0 and §6.3 — the interruption budget. This is the object that makes 'not too many notifications' testable rather than a matter of taste. A silent divergence here is invisible until it is a review: one platform notifying weekly where the other notifies daily is the difference between a differentiator and an uninstall.

constants._proactive_note: 7 days. One Class C notification per week, across ALL C sources combined — not per source. Every re-engagement idea in the category lands in C, and this is the entire allowance.
constants._return_note: 90 days. Scenario 13's own cap, on top of the C budget. A return notice is the single most intrusive thing the app may say, so it is rationed twice.

classes.note: Class A. Something happened to the user's data or ride that they must know about. Unlimited, but each is rare by construction.
Class B. The user asked for this one, at a time they chose. Exactly what they asked for, no more and no less.
Class C. The app decided to speak. The only class the budget applies to.
Class D. A person at TrackMe needs to tell everyone something operational. Deliberately outside the C budget in BOTH directions — see the cases below.

allows.note: A ride finalized by the system is not rationed. Losing someone's ride silently is the worst outcome in the release.
The user set this reminder themselves. Suppressing it would be the app overruling a schedule the user can see and edit.
Never sent one. A fresh install is not owed a week of silence first.

Exactly 7 days. The boundary is inclusive — a weekly recap must be able to land on the same weekday it landed on last week, or it drifts a day later every week until it is arriving on a different day entirely.
One millisecond short. Off-by-one here is the difference between weekly and twice-weekly.

A last-sent timestamp in the future. Clock changes, restores from backup and timezone edits all produce this. Refusing is correct: the alternative is a device whose clock jumped backwards emitting a proactive notification every single launch until real time catches up.
Class D is not rationed by the C budget. A maintenance notice suppressed because a weekly recap went out on Tuesday is an outage nobody was told about.

ledger.description: sending a C advances the ledger
sending an A does not advance it
sending a B does not advance it
sending a D does not advance it — Class D must not become a way to mute Class C
a later C moves the ledger forward
an out-of-order C never moves it backwards — a backwards clock must not reopen the budget

proactive_priority.note: Scenario 13. Ranked above the recap because it is far rarer (once per 90 days at most) and because the recap it would lose to is, for a returning user, a report of a week in which they did nothing.
Scenario 8, the flagship C. Carries scenario 10a's level-proximity line, so the level fact ships without its own interruption.

choose.note: Nothing eligible. Not an error — most weeks are this.

Both eligible: one is chosen and the other is NOT consumed. It stays eligible for its next window, exactly as WeeklyRecapSelector already behaves. Skipping is free; that is what makes a one-per-week cap survivable instead of lossy.
Same set, other order in. The result must not depend on iteration order — a Set on one platform and an Array on the other is exactly how that divergence would arrive.

return_notice.note: Never sent one, and long enough away.

The 21-day boundary. HomeInsight.Return computes at 14 days in-app; the notification threshold is deliberately higher than the in-app one, because interrupting someone is a bigger claim than showing them something when they open the app.
Twenty days is a holiday, not a lapse.
Exactly 90 days since the last one.
One millisecond short of 90 days. Two return notices in a quarter is nagging someone about not exercising, which §4.2 N2 rules out.
They came back. The 90-day window is open again but there is nothing to say — and saying it anyway is how a return notice becomes a streak reminder.
